method.label: Calculate each rider’s time by leg

annotationRationale: Distance divided by the appropriate directional speed gives each leg’s time. Fraction arithmetic combines the times, and time-unit conversion gives the requested difference in minutes.
sourceMethod: Follows the official separate time totals for Minnie and Penny, making Penny’s reversed terrain explicit and showing the common-denominator arithmetic.

review.mathCheck: Reversing direction swaps uphill and downhill. Minnie takes \(7/2\) hours; Penny takes \(20/30+15/10+10/40=29/12\) hours. Their difference is \(13/12\) hours, or 65 minutes, choice C.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Originally worded, faithful expansion of MAA solution 9 on page 3: reverse the slopes, sum distance/speed for each rider, subtract, and convert to minutes.
review.annotationCheck: The rate relationship is correctly assessed; fraction arithmetic and time conversion are appropriate support. All route legs, directional speeds, and units are explicit.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The three accepted CN links match the speed-time-distance relationship, mixed fraction arithmetic, and hour-minute conversion; the latter two are supporting knowledge.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: 6.RP.A.3b supports constant-speed calculations. 6.RP.A.2 and 7.RP.A.1 are partial rate crosswalks; fractional-input unit rates are unused. 5.NF.A.2 supports unlike-denominator sums, while 4.NF.B.3c is only partial because it specifies like denominators. 4.MD.A.1 and 5.MD.A.1 support conversion.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: cnm_p111 fits obtaining time from distance and speed; cnm_p174 fits adding and subtracting fractional times; cnm_p062 fits multiplying hours by 60.
